reconciliation_findings.title: E-Transit Loan - 4140: an extra principal payment around 2026-08-10
reconciliation_findings.plain_english: Between 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-10 this loan's balance fell $5,000.00, but the scheduled payment is only $1,180.32 — $3,819.68 more principal came off than the regular payment explains. That is almost always a deliberate extra principal payment. It matters because a period's interest is worked out as payment minus principal: with the extra payment folded in, the interest comes out negative, which is impossible and cannot be booked. Two readings fit these numbers and only you can say which is right: either the extra payment was $5,000.00 and the regular payment fell outside this window, or it was $3,819.68 alongside a regular payment inside it.

reconciliation_findings.title: PayPal: balance is measured differently from the ledger
reconciliation_findings.plain_english: The most recent balance on file for this loan comes from its amortization schedule dated 2026-07-29, and that figure is a total payback amount ($64,879.69). The Xero ledger records this loan on a principal-only basis. Those two measure different things — a total-payback figure still includes fees or interest not yet earned, so it will always read higher than the principal actually owed. Any automatic comparison between them will show a difference that is not a real error. This is almost certainly why this loan has looked out of balance.

proposed_action.note: Either record a principal-only balance for this loan (importing the lender's own transaction history does this), or convert before comparing: principal = total_payback balance minus the unearned fee remaining at that date. Do not "fix" the difference by adjusting the ledger — the ledger is not wrong.
